yaml.title: morph_autocorrelation
yaml.description: Lag-1 autocorrelation of morphological traits along a geographic gradient

markdown.markdown:
```{r}
#| eval: false
moRphoTaxa::morph_autocorrelation()
```


Measures, for each morphological trait, how similar the values of
neighbouring specimens are when specimens are ordered along a
geographic axis (latitude or longitude) or kept in their original
spreadsheet order. A positive lag-1 autocorrelation indicates that
specimens close to each other in the ordering tend to have similar
values (a gradient or geographic structure in the trait), a value near
zero indicates no ordering-related structure, and a negative value
indicates that neighbouring specimens tend to alternate.

Takes the morphometric matrix produced by `morph_matrix_setting()` and,
when specimens are ordered by geography, the geographical matrix
produced by `geo_matrix_setting()`. For each requested trait block, the
function computes the autocorrelation of every trait, draws a ranked
bar chart, and writes a combined summary table.

### Details

**Ordering specimens.**
Specimens are matched by row names (the specimen identifiers shared by
`morph_matrix_setting()` and `geo_matrix_setting()`) and sorted once,
before any block is analyzed:

- `"latitude"` (default): ascending `decimalLatitude`;
- `"longitude"`: ascending `decimalLongitude`;
- `"none"`: the row order of `analysis_data` is kept (the spreadsheet order, e.g. collection number). `geodata` is not needed in this case.

When ordering by latitude or longitude, specimens of `analysis_data`
that are absent from `geodata` (or have a missing coordinate) are
dropped. Specimens with identical coordinates keep their relative
spreadsheet order.

**Lag-1 autocorrelation.**
For each trait, the specimens are taken in the chosen order and the
trait value of each specimen is correlated with the value of the
preceding specimen, using the coefficient given by `cor_method`.
A pair of consecutive specimens is used only if both have a measured
value for that trait; the autocorrelation is `NA`, and the trait is
left out of the results, when fewer than 3 such pairs exist or when
the trait is constant among them. The coefficient is descriptive: no
significance test is performed. It only detects structure along the
chosen ordering axis.

**Pooled taxa.**
All specimens in `analysis_data` are ordered together. If several
taxa are included and they occupy different parts of the ordering axis,
differences between taxa contribute to the autocorrelation. To examine
geographic structure within a single taxon, build `analysis_data`
with `species_selected` set to that taxon in
`morph_matrix_setting()`.

**Trait blocks.**
The vegetative (`"veg"`), floral (`"flo"`), and fruit
(`"fru"`) trait blocks are read from the `"base_cols"`
attribute of `analysis_data`, created by `morph_matrix_setting()`.
With `blocks = "all"`, each available block is run, followed by
every combination of two or more available blocks, named by
concatenating the block names (`"vegflo"`, `"vegfru"`,
`"flofru"`, `"vegflofru"`). Any single block or combination
can also be requested by name. Because the autocorrelation is computed
trait by trait, a trait has the same value in every block that contains
it; combined blocks only group traits in a single chart and table.

**Outputs.**
One chart per block (`Autocorrelation_<block>.<ext>`) and a single
`Autocorrelation_summary.csv` with all blocks are written to a
dated subfolder (`format(Sys.time(), "%d%b%Y")`) inside
`"Figs_Autocorrelation"`. The dated subfolder means repeated runs
do not overwrite each other. Trait labels in the charts and the summary
are the descriptive part of the column name, with underscores replaced
by spaces (`"petiole_length/PETIlng"` becomes
`"petiole length"`); columns already renamed to codes are shown as
they are.

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| analysis_data | A data frame produced by `morph_matrix_setting()`, with specimen identifiers as row names and the `"base_cols"` attribute. Do not strip attributes (e.g. by subsetting or rebuilding the data frame) before calling this function. |
| geodata | A data frame produced by `geo_matrix_setting()`, with specimen identifiers as row names and the `decimalLatitude` and `decimalLongitude` columns. Required when `order_by` is `"latitude"` or `"longitude"`; ignored when `order_by = "none"`. Default is `NULL`. |
| blocks | Character vector of blocks to analyze. `"all"` (default) runs every available block and every combination of blocks. Otherwise, one or more of `"veg"`, `"flo"`, `"fru"`, `"vegflo"`, `"vegfru"`, `"flofru"`, and `"vegflofru"`, restricted to the blocks available in `analysis_data`. Unavailable names are ignored with a warning. |
| cor_method | Character string giving the correlation coefficient used for the lag-1 autocorrelation. One of `"pearson"` (default), `"spearman"`, or `"kendall"`. Passed to `stats::cor()`. |
| order_by | Character string giving how specimens are ordered before computing the autocorrelation. One of `"latitude"` (default), `"longitude"`, or `"none"` (keep the row order of `analysis_data`). |
| file_formats | Character vector specifying the file formats used to save the charts. One or more of `"pdf"` and `"jpg"`. Default is `c("pdf", "jpg")`. |
| verbose | Logical. If `TRUE` (default), prints progress messages and, for each block, the number of traits computed and the traits with the highest and lowest autocorrelation. |

### Value

A list, returned invisibly, with the elements:

`results`A data frame with one row per trait and block,
with columns `block`, `trait`, and `autocor`, or
`NULL` if no block produced results.
`plots`A named list of `ggplot2::ggplot()` objects, one per
block.
`specimen_order`Character vector of specimen identifiers in
the order used.
`output_dir`Path of the folder where the charts and the
summary table were saved.

The function is also called for its side effects: charts and the summary
table are written to `output_dir`.

### Examples

```r
# Both matrices must be built from the same specimens
geo <- geo_matrix_setting(
  xlsx_path = "specimen_data.xlsx",
  taxon_col = "species",
  edaphic = FALSE
)

morph <- morph_matrix_setting(
  xlsx_path = "specimen_data.xlsx",
  taxon_col = "species",
  trait_name_type = "code",
  veg_first = "petiole_length/PETIlng",
  flo_first = "inflorescence_length/INFLlng",
  fru_first = "fruit_stipe_length/FRSTlng"
)

# Every block and block combination, specimens ordered by latitude
res <- morph_autocorrelation(analysis_data = morph, geodata = geo)
head(res$results)

# Floral traits only, ordered by longitude, Spearman correlation
res <- morph_autocorrelation(
  analysis_data = morph,
  geodata = geo,
  blocks = "flo",
  cor_method = "spearman",
  order_by = "longitude"
)

# Keep the original spreadsheet order (geodata not needed)
res <- morph_autocorrelation(
  analysis_data = morph,
  blocks = c("veg", "fru"),
  order_by = "none",
  file_formats = "pdf"
)
```
